svg.title: The Fable 5.1 ceiling of 66 holds after three flagships ship in 48 hours, while a second frontier — agentic, computer-use and cyber — splits off under GPT-6 Astra
svg.desc: A two-part chart covering September 2 to 5, 2026. On the left, a horizontal bar chart of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at max effort on version 4.1.1 shows that the ceiling held: Claude Fable 5.1 stays number one at 66, unchanged from September 1, above Claude Opus 5 at 63, Meta's new Muse Spark 1.3 at 62 released September 2, OpenAI's new GPT-6 Astra at 61 released September 3 which merely ties its own predecessor GPT-5.6 Sol also at 61. Three flagships shipped in forty-eight hours and none retook the top. A note records that Artificial Analysis rushed out Intelligence Index version 4.2 on September 5, rescaling the top to Fable 5.1 at 57 and GPT-6 Astra second at 55. On the right, a callout headed the frontier splits explains that GPT-6 Astra does not lead general intelligence but sets a new frontier on a different axis: computer use on OSWorld version 2 at 72.6 percent up from 65.7, Terminal-Bench 4.0 coding at 57.7 percent ahead of Fable 5.1 at 55.8, a perfect 100 percent on ExploitBench as the first model OpenAI rates Critical for cyber under its Preparedness Framework, and it finishes a task for under half the token cost of Fable 5.1. A footer states the through-line: governance by tier now has a third lab. Anthropic ships Fable with a vetted Mythos sibling, Z.ai ships GLM-5.3-Flash open with a revenue-gated flagship license, and now OpenAI ships GPT-6 Astra generally available with offensive-cyber tasks refused, opening the more permissive tier only through its vetted Daybreak program which got access first. Meanwhile Google shipped yet another Flash, Gemini 3.8 Flash, while Gemini 3.5 Pro missed another target and stays the lone frozen frontier thread.
svg.text: The 66 ceiling HOLDS — three flagships in 48h, none retook #1 — but the frontier SPLITS
Sep 2–5: Meta Muse Spark 1.3, OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, Google Gemini 3.8 Flash all ship — Fable 5.1 (Sep 1) stays the top of the Index
General Intelligence Index (AA v4.1.1, max)

Sep 5: AA rushes out Index v4.2 (interim, more agentic) — rescales top to
Fable 5.1 57 (#1) · GPT-6 Astra 55 (#2). Fable stays #1 on both rulers.
The frontier SPLITS — GPT-6 Astra leads a DIFFERENT axis
Not the general Index — but agentic / computer-use / cyber:
Computer use (OSWorld v2): 72.6% vs Sol 65.7 · ½ the time
Terminal-Bench 4.0 (coding): 57.7% > Fable 5.1 55.8
ExploitBench: 100% · SRE-Bench 88% · found 2 zero-days
Token cost/task: < ½ of Fable 5.1 — efficiency jump
First model OpenAI rates "Critical" for cyber
(Preparedness Framework — Sol was "High"). Release delayed
to add safeguards; GA refuses PoC-exploit generation.
The through-line holds: governance BY TIER now has a THIRD lab
Anthropic — Fable 5.1 (GA) + Mythos 5.1 (vetted cyber/bio access)
Z.ai — GLM-5.3-Flash (MIT, open) + flagship (open weights, $10B-revenue review trigger)
OpenAI (NEW) — GPT-6 Astra (GA, offensive-cyber refused) + Daybreak (vetted defenders — got access FIRST)
Still frozen — Google. Shipped a 4th Flash (Gemini 3.8 Flash, Sep 2) while Gemini 3.5 Pro missed another target — the lone frozen frontier thread.
